quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane. You need to merge.

questions.question: In Iowa, is it illegal for any driver to read, write, or send a text message while driving?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Yes, it is illegal. In Iowa, drivers cannot read, write, or send text messages while driving. You must stop your vehicle safely off the road before using a phone to text.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, slow down, move out of the way, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: If a vehicle has airbags, should you still wear a seat belt?

options.text: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
No, seat belts are not needed.
Seat belts should be worn behind your back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, seat belts should still be worn.
questions.explanation: Airbags and seat belts work together. Always wear your seat belt, even if your vehicle has airbags. Both provide the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: First, use your turn signal. Then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure the path is clear before you change lanes.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the effect of the alcohol.
The alcohol helps the medicine work better.
The combination can increase the effects of both.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with medicine can increase how much each substance affects you. One drink with cold medicine could affect you like having several drinks without medicine.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, what is important to remember?

options.text: Trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Trucks can pass faster going downhill than smaller vehicles.
Trucks have a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Trucks can pass faster going uphill than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Because trucks are large and heavy, they need more space to stop than smaller vehicles do.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Always follow the crossing guard's directions in a school zone. Be ready to slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?

options.text: Loosely.
Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
Hidden under the seat.
So the warning buzzer does not go off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snugly across your hip bones and lower belly.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hip bones and lower belly. The shoulder belt should be comfortable so you can fit your fist between it and your chest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead. Be ready for traffic coming from other directions.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work whenever you drive.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road.
Driving too fast for the conditions.
Following other vehicles too closely.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Driving too fast causes crashes. Not paying attention can lead to hitting other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Signaling your intentions before turning, changing lanes, or driving away from a curb:

options.text: Is necessary only if other traffic is present.
Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
Is necessary only during the maneuver, not before.
Is not necessary if the maneuver is done slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good driving habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, a driver should yield the right-of-way.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Pedestrians with disabilities who use a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device have the right-of-way on sidewalks and roadways. They have the same rights as all other pedestrians.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: Just like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:

options.text: Help you to be a better driver.
Make you feel better.
Impair your judgment.

questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and weakens judgment just like drugs and alcohol.

questions.question: If you are involved in a serious motor vehicle crash:

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Determine if anyone is injured.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. Check if anyone is hurt. Call 911 if someone is injured. Report the crash to police if there is an injury, death, or property damage over $1,000.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a hospital emergency room is located to the right.

questions.question: Because there is often slow-moving traffic on county highways, you should:

options.text: Stay in the left lane and drive above the speed limit.
Be ready to adjust your speed to the speed of traffic.
Pass slow-moving vehicles when in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to adjust your speed to the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: Look ahead to spot slow-moving vehicles early. This gives you time to change lanes or slow down safely. Always match the speed of traffic, but stay within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, wait until you can see the entire car in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When passing, do not return to your original lane until you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers to be careful when the road is wet and slippery.

questions.question: Adjust your rearview and side mirrors:

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before driving to keep yourself and others safe. Before moving your vehicle, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt, and secure loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Anything that requires you to ____ could cause you to crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended, you should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when you think most children are done leaving the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop signal on. Do not proceed until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up so you can turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn from this lane.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected green arrow is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Stare directly ahead of their car.
Only focus on the middle of the road.
Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind their car.
questions.explanation: Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind your car. Good drivers know what is happening all around their vehicle.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
Pull to the right and drive around the pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross the street.
questions.explanation: You must let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk. Wait until the intersection is clear before you proceed.

questions.question: Before driving, a driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the drug labels to check for warnings.
Drink alcohol instead.
Drive anyway, regardless of warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the drug labels to check for warnings.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medications can affect your driving. Check labels on cold and allergy medicines for warnings. If unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of concentration.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol damages your vision, judgment, concentration, and coordination.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to make an emergency stop on an interstate?

options.text: Honk your horn to get the attention of other drivers.
Get out of your car and wave down the next vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder of an interstate or highway, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if you can. Traffic moves very fast on interstates, so it is dangerous to stand or walk on the shoulder.

questions.question: Construction work zone signs are orange in color.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Work zone signs are usually orange and diamond-shaped. Some are rectangular. Many of these signs are reflective so you can see them better at night.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off moisture in the air and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: When roads are wet, snowy, or icy, your tires do not grip the road as well as they do on dry roads. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you continue.
